items.title: Eddie Metz Jr. interviewed by Monk Rowe, New Hartford, New York, October 3, 2015
items.q: The piano player, Tom Hook, he’s looking at me.

ctx.x: Well you’ve got all these great gigs you’ve played. And this is a sort of a hard question. Do you recall your worst gig ever?

Boy oh boy. There could be a whole bunch of them. A couple of gigs I learned my lesson early to not overindulge. Especially drinking. I don’t drink anymore and I never had a problem with it, I just don’t care for it anymore the way it makes you feel. A couple of times with the rock band getting a little too drunk to play and they were my good buddies, we’d played together for a long time. The piano player, Tom Hook, he’s looking at me. I’m going “I’m sorry.” He’s like, “hey get out of here.” And he finished the…

time. People see the drums coming in and they do not sit near the bandstand and they don’t understand that I could probably play drums quieter than anybody. You know? So worst gigs would have been more like dealing with food and beverage managers instead of the other musicians.
